content:
Is there a canonical, Mathlib-style way to define/work with a weighted graph? I see that the Graph structure allows an arbitrary edge set, which I guess could be a set of weights, but then it seems that two edges wouldn't be able to have the same weight.

I'm asking because I'm working on formalizing some content from the very beginning of this textbook, and although I have my own formalization that follows the book very closely, I'd like to be able to rely on Mathlib as much as possible.

docs#SimpleGraph.EdgeLabeling

Cool! Are you planning to contribute stuff to Mathlib along the way? We don't have anything on weights/flows/cuts at the moment (#34028 was an attempt but it's abandoned)

Also you might like to depend on other people's graph theory libraries, such as https://vbeffara.github.io/Graphs/ by Vincent Beffara

Thank you for pointing out docs#SimpleGraph.EdgeLabeling! I'll see if I can use it to simplify my implementation.

Snir Broshi said:

Cool! Are you planning to contribute stuff to Mathlib along the way? We don't have anything on weights/flows/cuts at the moment (#34028 was an attempt but it's abandoned)

I'd like to. Do you know who might be interested in reviewing a PR like this? (Are you a Mathlib reviewer by chance?) I've already upstreamed a couple minor lemmas that I though would be more broadly useful in #40201, and if I encounter any more that don't require new definitions, I'll definitely try to upstream them too. But, for new definitions, it would be a lot of work for a reviewer, and I have a long way to go before my code will be review-ready.

Snir Broshi said:

Also you might like to depend on other people's graph theory libraries, such as https://vbeffara.github.io/Graphs/ by Vincent Beffara

This repo seems cool, but as far as I can tell at a first glance, its content is largely disjoint from what I'm trying to formalize. Thank you for sharing it though!

Gregory Wickham said:

(Are you a Mathlib reviewer by chance?)

No sorry, though I tend to review graph theory PRs which hopefully helps them get merged faster :)

Gregory Wickham said:

But, for new definitions, it would be a lot of work for a reviewer, and I have a long way to go before my code will be review-ready.

FWIW I think we (graph theory contributors) should work on PRing definitions (e.g. cuts/flows/perfect-graphs/dominating-sets/etc), but I agree they are a lot of work for all the people involved.

Good luck!

Snir Broshi said:

No sorry, though I tend to review graph theory PRs which hopefully helps them get merged faster :)

In that case, I made draft PR (#40495) with some of the initial definitions and API I've formalized. Any feedback would be appreciated (especially if you have a way to golf the proof of associatedForm_neq_basisFuns_eq_neq_edgeWeight). A lot of the math may seem a bit strange, but that's because I'm working from a book that focuses on graph Laplacians, Dirichlet forms, and spectral theory so that's really what I'm trying to formalize.

Over the next few days I plan to make many improvements to the code and documentation, so there is definitely no rush to take a look at it.
